parts:
Hi

the results$marginal... gives for each location (or space-time
location depending on the model), the marginal distribution for
'ID.area'. results$summary... is just a computed summary of this
marginal distribution, in terms of mean, sd, and quantiles.

Best
H

On Fri, 2020-04-10 at 16:08 -0700, madhura rane wrote:
> Hello,
>
> I fit a space-time interaction model for an infectious disease. I
> have 397 areas (census tracts) and 19 years of data. The data is
> quite sparse with plenty of zeros in the I*T matrix.
>
> The main purpose of this exercise is disease mapping. I would like
> map disease risk smoothed in space and time over 19 years. My
> question is: should I plot the results$marginals.random$ID.area
> (marginal random effects) or mod.intI$summary.random$ID.area (summary
> of random effects)? I have seen both used to display heterogeneity in
> spatial risk.
